newsitem.title: CANADA: Gulf Canada offshore drilling plans on hold.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Canada offshore drilling plans on hold.

text.p: Plans by Gulf Canada Resources Ltd for exploration in waters that straddle Canadian and French territory off Canada's east coast are on hold until two Canadian provinces iron out their common border, a Gulf spokesman said on Monday.

Gulf wants to explore for oil on about five million acres south of the French islands of St. Pierre and Miquelon off Newfoundland's southwest coast, Gulf Spokesman Dennis Martin said in a telephone interview.

Canada and France agreed to a border separating the small French islands from Canadian territory in 1996, but the provinces of Newfoundland and Nova Scotia must still agree to the location of their common border, Martin said.
"We're still sort of in the waiting mode," he said. "It's a big chunk of land in a pretty hot area, so obviously we'd like that to happen sooner than later."
The Canada-France border cuts through the exploration lands, and Gulf plans to apply for permits from both nations before starting seismic work.
Gulf picked up rights to the huge acreage in the late 1960s, and recent booming oil exploration activity off Canada's east coast convinced it to return to operations in the region, Martin said.
Gulf also has a stake in the planned White Rose development off Newfoundland led by Husky Oil Ltd.

The company pulled out of the Hibernia project, Canada's first major east coast offshore development, in the early 1990s as construction on its platform was getting under way. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
